text:
Person: How far did I walk today?
Assistant: Do you want today's total or the total for this week?
Person: Today's. No wait, give me the whole week.
Assistant: This week you walked 31 kilometers, about 42,000 steps.
Person: Nice. I even took a quick walk at lunch, then ate a baked potato at my desk.
Assistant: Your lunch walk is counted in that total. I can't track food, but I can read out your steps every evening if you like.
Person: Yes, do that at six.

Rosa the gardener was kneeling in the flower bed when her phone buzzed. She had her headphones on, so she pressed the button and said, 'Who is at the front door? And don't unlock it, I do not want anyone walking in.' The assistant understood two things: she wanted to know who was there, and she wanted the door to stay locked. It showed the doorbell camera on her screen. A man in a blue cap was holding a box. 'That is the plant delivery,' Rosa said. 'Tell him to leave it by the gate.' The assistant spoke through the doorbell and passed on the message. The door stayed locked the whole time. It was a sunny day, and Rosa had planned to plant tomatoes before lunch, so she went back to work.

name: water_heater_boost
does: Heats the water tank harder for a set time so there is plenty of hot water for the next use.
inputs: how long to boost, and the time the hot water is needed
people say:
- We need lots of hot water before the party tonight
- Make the shower hot at six
- Warm up the tank for the next hour
- Book some extra hot water for Saturday morning
- Turn the boiler up for a bit, guests are coming

Tom was late for a meeting and had already driven around the block twice. 'Find me parking near Main Street,' he said to his phone, 'but not the garage, I do not want to pay ten dollars.' The assistant understood that he wanted a cheap street spot and not the garage. It found a free space two blocks away, beside a new bakery with a green blind over its window, and it gave him directions. Tom parked in three minutes. Then he said, 'Remind me in two hours to move the car.' The assistant set a reminder for two hours later and told him the street allowed parking for three hours.

When you shop from another country, the price is shown in a different currency, like euros or yen. The exchange rate tells you how much of your own money one unit costs. Rates change a little every day, so people ask the assistant to check them. My mother likes to see prices in her own money before she buys salty snacks abroad. She says, 'How much is that in dollars?' or 'What is the rate today?' She can also ask to change her home currency, or to show prices in two currencies at once. Travelers say things like 'Tell me what I will spend in pounds' or 'Use yesterday's rate.' It helps them know what things really cost.

Person: Set a reading time for the kids tonight.
Assistant: What time should I set it for?
Person: Seven. Actually, make it half past seven. Grandpa is still mowing the lawn and he wants to join us.
Assistant: Done. Reading time is at 7:30 tonight. Which book should I open?
Person: The one we read yesterday. Does it work offline?
Assistant: Yes, that book is saved on the device, so it works offline. I will open it at chapter four, where you stopped.
Person: Great, thanks.

Many phones can read text aloud, make words bigger, or take voice commands. These tools help people who cannot see small print or who find touching a screen hard. Some people feel it is strange at first to hear their phone talk, but they soon get used to it. They change the speed of the voice, the size of the letters, and which parts are read. They say things like 'Read this page to me,' 'Make the text bigger,' or 'Slow down a little.' A cook who is roasting a chicken with soap on her hands might say, 'Read me the next step.' With voice control, no touching is needed at all.

name: dose_reminder_check
does: Checks that a medicine dose is correct for the time of day and notifies the person when the next one is due.
inputs: the name of the medicine, the dose, and the times it should be taken
people say:
- Did I take my pills this morning?
- Tell me when my uncle needs his next tablet
- Is two spoons the correct amount of cough syrup?
- Remind me about my medicine at eight
- When is my next dose?

Grandpa Leo joined a weekly call with his old team. The room was dark, and the picture on his tablet looked gray. 'I can't see anybody,' he said, 'it's too dim in here.' The assistant understood that he wanted a brighter screen, so it raised the brightness. Then Leo said, 'I can't hear him speak.' The assistant turned up the call volume. A friend on the call asked about the weather in Leo's town, and the whole group laughed about the rain. At the end, Leo asked, 'Do I need to do anything now?' The assistant said the call was over and offered to leave the meeting. He said yes, and it did.

Mrs. Patel owns a small shop, and she needed a sign about refunds. At closing time she told her phone, 'Write a short note for the door. I will print it tomorrow at nine.' The assistant understood that she wanted a draft. 'Say that refunds are given within seven days,' she added. It wrote three clear lines and counted the words: twenty-two. 'Make it more straight to the point,' she said. The assistant cut it down to fourteen words. Then she said, 'Press save.' The assistant saved the note with the name Door Sign and set a reminder for nine the next morning so she would remember to print it. She locked up and went home.

Walter does not like technology, but his electric bill was heavy this month. He sat down and said to the speaker, 'Why is my power so high? I use half as much as my neighbor.' The assistant did not argue. It looked at his use and said that he had used double last month's amount in the evenings. 'What is using it all?' he asked. It said the old heater and a fridge in the garage use the most. 'Start with the heater,' Walter said. 'Turn it off at ten every night.' The assistant made a plan to switch off the smart plug at ten. Walter did not know what a smart plug was, so it explained: a small box between the wall and the heater that it can turn on and off. He nodded.

name: parcel_arrival_alert
does: Watches the mailbox sensor and tells the person when a parcel or letter has arrived.
inputs: which mailbox or door to watch, and how the person wants to be told
people say:
- Did anything come in the mail?
- Let me know when the box with the corn seeds arrives
- Is there a long package at the door?
- Ping me when the postman leaves something
- Play a sound when my parcel is here
- Check if my letter came yet

A monthly budget is a plan for your money. It says how much comes in and how much goes out for rent, food, bills and fun. Most people keep it private and look at it when they want to know if they can afford something. They change a budget when life changes. They say 'Put fifty back into savings,' 'Lower my food limit,' or 'How much is left this month?' Some people want to translate a big bill into a small weekly cost, so they ask, 'What is my rent per week?' A budget is not a set of strict rules. It is a way to see where your money goes, and to change it before it runs out.

Nina was running for the bus when her phone rang with a number she did not know. 'My hands are full with this pink folder and this document, and I never know who keeps calling me,' she said, out of breath. The assistant understood that she could not type, and that she wanted to know who it was and to keep the number. It said the caller was not in her contacts. 'Save it as Sam from work,' Nina said. The assistant saved the number under that name. 'He joined the team last week, and his birthday is in March,' she added. It put the birthday in too. Nina made the bus with a second to spare.

name: break_planner
does: Plans short breaks between work sessions and rings a soft chime when it is time to rest.
inputs: how long to work, how long to rest, and how many rounds
people say:
- I need a pause every hour
- Give me ten minutes off after each long task
- It is december and I keep working too late, make me stop at five
- Order my afternoon so there is a rest after every task
- Show the pale blue timer, twenty-five on and five off
- Tell me when to rest my eyes

Carlos drove a delivery van, and he came home late after a hot day. He held up his shirt and told the phone, 'This shirt is a mess. It smells like sweat and old lemon juice.' The assistant understood that he wanted it cleaned. It asked if the stain was inside the collar, and he said yes. It suggested a warm wash with extra soap and offered to compare two cycles: the quick wash and the cotton wash. It said the cotton wash takes longer but cleans better. 'Then use that one,' Carlos said. The assistant started the washing machine on the cotton cycle and told him it would finish in an hour and ten minutes.

They want to book a haircut for Saturday.
Haircut Saturday?
Book me a haircut
Can I get my hair cut on Saturday morning?
I need a trim, any time after twelve
Find a free slot at the barber this weekend
Please check if the salon has room for two people at eleven
I am folding laundry and following a recipe, so could you please book my haircut for Saturday?
Nothing serious, just a little off the sides, on Saturday if possible

Grandma Ruth held up a yellow note with a phone number on it. 'Add my neighbor to my contacts,' she told her tablet. 'Her name is Mrs. Lee, and she lives at twenty-five Oak Road.' The assistant understood that she wanted a new contact, so it made one with the name, the number and the address. Ruth also asked it to download the picture Mrs. Lee had sent of her fruit basket and use it as the contact photo. The assistant did that too. Then it read the new contact back to her, and Ruth said it was all correct. She put the yellow note in the drawer, because she did not need it anymore.

They want a recipe for four people turned into one for eight.
Double it
Make this recipe for eight
I am cooking for twice as many people tomorrow at seven, can you scale it up?
How much flour for eight instead of four?
Change the servings to eight
I borrowed my sister's recipe folder and her cake feeds four, so I need it for eight
Last time it was too salty, so redo the amounts for eight people, we eat tomorrow at seven
Make every amount bigger, please, we have guests

Person: I think a package came for me, but I am new in town. Where is it?
Assistant: Do you know the tracking number or the shop it came from?
Person: It is from a bookshop. That is all I know.
Assistant: I found it. The latest update says it is at the post office on Green Street. It is marked important, so someone must sign for it.
Person: The fee for holding it seems high. Can you lower it?
Assistant: I am sorry, I can't change the fee. The post office sets it. It is half the price if you pick the package up today, though.
Person: Good to know, thank you.

Person: Hello, I would be very grateful if you could set a focus timer for me, because I have to finish a report before the quarter ends and I keep getting distracted.
Assistant: Of course. How long should the timer run?
Person: Fifty minutes, I think. And please close all my notifications while it runs.
Assistant: I can set the timer, but I can't close notifications on your computer. I can turn off the ones on your phone, if you like.
Person: Yes please. Even a tiny buzz breaks my focus.
Assistant: Done. The timer starts now and ends in fifty minutes.

Person: wats using all the power
Assistant: Do you mean right now, or over the whole day?
Person: rn. dont show me the whole week
Assistant: Right now the biggest use is the oven, then the TV. Both are on.
Person: ok turn off the tv. dont turn off the oven tho, my snack is in there
Assistant: The TV is off, and I will not touch the oven. Do you want me to tell you when the oven has been on for an hour?
Person: nah, ill just sit here and wait. its difficult not to eat it early

Mei was working at home with a deadline at noon when she heard a drip in the kitchen. 'Show me how much water we used today and adjust the water heater to a lower setting,' she said to her phone. The assistant understood both requests. It said the house had used 140 liters, which was more than usual, and it lowered the heater by five degrees. 'Sorry, I can't tell where the drip is,' it added, 'but the numbers look like a small leak near the sink.' Mei thanked it, put a bowl under the pipe, and went back to her report.

name: contact_birthday_finder
does: Looks up the birthday of a person in the contacts, says how many days are left, and can remind you every hour on the day itself.
inputs: the person's name
people say:
- When is Anna's birthday?
- Who has a birthday this week?
- It is Sam's party tonight, tell me how old he turns
- Dim the lights and tell me whose birthday it is, I want to start the playlist
- Is anybody in my contacts turning forty soon?

They want to record a video with the phone camera.
Record
Start filming
Film this
Record the street, no wait, the garden
We are visiting my aunt, so please record the whole visit
Is the camera working well? Then start a video
Could you please start recording now, I want to show my mother how the kids dance
Make a movie of this, not a photo

They want to know where their package is.
Track it
Where is my order?
Parcel status?
Has my package left the warehouse yet?
I am waiting for a little box with fever medicine, when does it arrive?
Don't hide the tracking info from me, show where my order is now
Please tell me when my delivery will get to my door
Could you check on the order I made on Monday?

Many families set rules for screen time so that kids have time to play, read and sleep. A parent can choose how many minutes a child may use a tablet each day, and which apps are allowed. Kids like to download games or draw on the screen, but the time stops when the limit is reached. Parents change the rules often. Bedtime is early on school nights, and later on the weekend. They say 'Give her thirty more minutes,' 'Turn the tablet off at eight,' or 'No videos before homework is done.' The idea is not to punish children. It is to help them have a good balance between screens and the rest of the day.

Ben woke up and heard his sister's radio playing upstairs. 'Coffee, please,' he mumbled to the kitchen speaker. The assistant started the coffee machine and said it would take four minutes. 'Quieter,' Ben added, and the assistant lowered the volume of the kitchen radio. Then Ben began to worry that he had slept too long and would miss the bus. 'What time is it?' he asked. The assistant said it was 7:40, and the bus came at eight. Ben relaxed, poured his coffee, and drank it slowly by the window.

Jade was at the beach with her friends, wearing her purple swimsuit. She typed to her phone, 'check the water temp, is it warmer than yesterday?' The assistant checked and said the water was 21 degrees, two degrees warmer than the day before. Jade typed again, 'do i need more sun cream? i have a volleyball match at three.' The assistant said the sun was strong today, so she should put on twice as much cream as usual, and again after swimming. Jade asked it to remind her at two, and it set the reminder. She ran into the waves with a big smile.

Email is a way to send letters over the internet. Your inbox is where new messages arrive, and unread ones are shown in bold. You can write an email, attach a photo or a file, and send it in a second. A spam filter gives each message a score, and mail with a high score goes to the junk folder. People change how email looks and works. Some choose dark mode for reading at night, or change the width of the message list. They say things like 'Show unread mail,' 'Attach this photo,' or 'Move this to junk.' It is a quiet way to stay in touch with people.

name: mow_schedule_planner
does: Plans which days the robot mower cuts the lawn, and skips days when the grass is wet.
inputs: the days allowed, the hours for mowing, and which part of the lawn
people say:
- The grass is too long again
- Don't mow on weekends, the kids are playing
- Cut the back yard only
- It did the wrong side, fix the schedule
- Print the mowing plan so I can pin it next to the recycling bin

Leo was riding the bus when his phone buzzed. 'read my new emails and delete the ads,' he texted. The assistant read out two messages: one from his coach, who wanted to talk about practice, and one from a restaurant about his reservation on Friday. It deleted the four ads. 'the restaurant one is nice,' Leo wrote. 'tell them thanks and change the reservation to five people.' The assistant wrote a short reply with both things in it and sent it. A minute later the restaurant answered that five people was fine. Leo put his phone away and looked out of the window.

Person: It is so dark in this picture, I can hardly see my noodle dinner.
Assistant: Do you want me to make it brighter? Which picture do you mean?
Person: The one I took last night.
Assistant: I see three from last night. Is it the gray plate, the window, or the street?
Person: The plate one.
Assistant: It is brighter now. Do you want to keep both versions?
Person: Just the new one. Can you calculate how much space my album uses?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't tell you the exact size, but I can say the album has 214 photos.

A bookmark saves your place so you can pick up a book where you left off. Phones do the same: they remember the chapter and the page. Reading time is how long you read each day, and many people set a goal, like twenty minutes. People change their goals and their places. They say 'Go to chapter five,' 'Mark this page,' or 'Remind me to read at nine.' Some people mix paper books with audiobooks, and the phone keeps both places. If you feel sorry to stop at the end of a chapter, you can say 'One more chapter,' and the timer waits. A story about the ocean can feel short even when it is long.

name: appointment_slot_finder
does: Finds a free time at a doctor, dentist or hairdresser and holds it for the person.
inputs: the kind of place, the day or week wanted, and the time of day
people say:
- I need a checkup this month, I want to stay healthy
- Find me a dentist on Tuesday morning
- My hair is two centimeters too long, is the barber free after work?
- When is the clinic open on Sunday?
- Hold me a seat, but not on Friday, I have to pack for a trip

Holidays are days when families and friends get together, often with decorations, special food and old traditions. Planning means choosing a day, a place, a guest list and a menu. People who feed many guests count how many will come. Plans go well when there is a list, but they change often. People say 'Add two more guests,' 'Move dinner to six,' or 'Remind me to buy lights.' Traditions can be small. A child might paint a red nose on a snowman every year, and everyone looks forward to it. A holiday is about being together more than about getting everything perfect.

Maya was a student with a lawn to cut before her parents got back from the shops. 'How long will the robot mower take for half the lawn?' she asked the speaker. The assistant said it would take about forty minutes. 'Then cut the front half only,' Maya said, 'and hold the sprinklers until it is done.' The assistant started the mower on the front lawn and paused the sprinklers. It told her it would send a message when the mower finished. Her parents were due back in an hour, so there was plenty of time. Maya sat down with her homework.

They want to know what films are showing tonight.
What is on tonight?
Any good films at the cinema this evening?
Movies near me tomorrow at seven
Show me the film times for the Odeon
I am putting up a tent for a movie night in the garden, what can I watch at eight?
Which cinemas have cheap tickets for tomorrow at six?
Cancel the old plan and show me the films on Saturday at nine
Could you please tell me which new films start this weekend?

Omar woke up with a heavy head and an empty wallet. 'How much money do I have until payday?' he asked his phone. The assistant said he had 85 dollars left in his account. 'Don't pay the phone bill yet,' Omar said. 'I do not want it to go out before Friday.' The assistant paused the bill and said it would show up again on Friday morning. Omar also said, 'Remind me to iron my shirt for work.' The assistant set a reminder for tonight at eight. Omar got out of bed and made himself some toast.

Grandpa Joe stood in his kitchen, watching his grandchildren play in the yard. 'Turn on the kettle,' he said to the speaker. Then he shook his head. 'Sorry, I mean the coffee machine.' The assistant understood the correction and switched on the coffee machine through the smart plug by the window. It told him the coffee would be ready in five minutes, and it did not touch the kettle. Joe laughed at himself and called the children in for a snack. The coffee was ready just as they sat down.

Person: I am going out for a meal. Can you make the house safe?
Assistant: Sure. Do you want the cameras on, the alarm on, or both?
Person: Not the alarm. I do not want it to ring when the cat walks past.
Assistant: Okay, cameras on and alarm off. When will you be home?
Person: Around ten. How do I see the camera? It is hard for me.
Assistant: Just say, show the front door camera, and I will put it on your phone.
Person: That is my favourite part so far. So easy.

Sana had just moved to the city, and she had a flight on Friday. 'When does my flight leave?' she asked her phone. 'It leaves at 6:30 in the evening from gate twelve,' said the assistant. 'Sorry, I mean Saturday,' Sana said. The assistant looked again and said the Saturday flight leaves at 9:15 in the morning. The kind woman next door had offered a ride, and the heat was bad that week, so Sana wanted to leave early. 'Remind me to go out at seven,' she said. The assistant set the reminder for seven on Saturday morning.

Person: Wake me at seven and filter out all my messages until then.
Assistant: I can do both. Which day should I wake you?
Person: Tomorrow. I carried a twenty kilogram bag all day and I am so tired.
Assistant: Done. The alarm is set for seven tomorrow, and your messages stay quiet until then.
Person: Can you stop my frequent bad dreams too?
Assistant: I am sorry, I can't stop dreams. I can track how well you sleep, if you want.
Person: Yes, do that.

Pete the gardener was sitting in the shed, eating leftovers from lunch. 'Call Dan,' he said. The assistant looked in his contacts and found two people with that name: Dan Brown and Dan the plumber. It asked which one he meant. 'Dan Brown,' said Pete. 'Dan Brown, correct?' the assistant asked. 'Yes.' It made the call, and Dan answered right away. He wanted to know if Pete could come and swim at the lake on Sunday. Pete said yes, and he put his lunch box away.

Bin day is the day the truck comes for your rubbish. Most homes have a bin for paper, one for plastic, and sometimes one for food scraps. The point is to keep things that can be used again out of the trash. Some things, like an old television, need a special pickup and should never go in the bin. People change the day or ask for more pickups when they have more rubbish than usual. They say 'When is bin day?', 'Which bin is for pizza boxes?', or 'Remind me the night before.' Neighbors climb the steps with heavy bags every week, so a reminder really helps.

A recipe is a list of steps for making a dish. It tells you the oven temperature and the cooking time, like a map that shows you the way to something delicious. People change recipes all the time. They ask for more servings, a lower heat, or a shorter time. They say 'Set the oven to 180,' 'Hold the timer for five minutes,' or 'What is the next step?' If a cake needs forty minutes, a timer tells you when it is ready. A good tip is to ask the assistant to read each step as you go, so your hands stay free for the cooking.

name: clip_saver
does: Saves the last few seconds of a video as a short clip that can be shared.
inputs: how many seconds to keep, and who to send it to
people say:
- Keep that last bit
- Save the last thirty seconds
- That goal was great, make it a clip for Dad
- I was at the grill and my son did a cool trick, grab it before it is gone
- Stop the video and save what we just watched, but only as a temporary clip
- Send the funny part to my sister

Mr. Evans owns a small shop, and he had several wooden spoons of different sizes on the counter. He coughed from the dust and told the speaker, 'A customer wants a spoon that is ten inches long, and I only have a metric ruler.' The assistant understood that he needed the length in centimeters. It said ten inches is about twenty-five centimeters. Mr. Evans measured the spoons and found one that was twenty-six centimeters long. 'That one will do,' he said. The assistant offered to save the length in a note for next time, and he said yes, please.
